ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p189/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p189/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p189/r13.claim: A report says the address to believing servants was revealed for Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib and his companions when they resolved to migrate to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p189/r13.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب وأصحابه حين عزموا على الهجرة إلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r1.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r1.claim: The main reading connects “in this life” to those who do good and promises them a great reward in the Hereafter, namely Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r1.anchor: والظاهر تعلق في هذه بأحسنوا، وأن المحسنين في الدنيا لهم في الآخرة حسنة، أي حسنة عظيمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r2.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r2.claim: Al-Suddi connects “in this life” to the reward itself: those who do good receive a good thing in this world, such as well-being, success, and God's protection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: في هذه من تمام حسنة، أي ولو تأخر لكان صفة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r3.claim: The call to migrate says God's land is wide; no one may excuse abandoning obedience by attachment to a homeland where it cannot be practiced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r3.anchor: وأرض الله واسعة، كقوله: ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r4.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r4.claim: ʿAta interprets the wide land as Medina, the destination of migration, and the good thing as relief from enemies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء: وأرض الله: المدينة للهجرة، قيل: فعلى هذا يكون أحسنوا: هاجروا، وحسنة: راحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r5.claim: Some identify God's wide land as Paradise; Ibn Atiyya calls this unsupported, while Abu Muslim argues it fits the surrounding promise of Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: أرض الله هنا: الجنة. قال ابن عطية: وهذا القول تحكم، لا دليل عليه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r6.claim: Abu Muslim argues that God's land can mean Paradise, citing its inheritance and its breadth as the home prepared for the God-fearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r6.anchor: لا يمتنع ذلك، لأنه تعالى أمر المؤمنين بالتقوى ثم بين أنه من اتقى له في الآخرة الحسنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r7.claim: A Prophetic report defines ihsan as worshipping God as though one sees Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r7.anchor: كما جاء: ما الإحسان؟ قال: أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r8.claim: Patient people receive reward without reckoning, meaning either they are not held to account or their reward is too abundant to count.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p190/r8.anchor: ذكر أن الصابرين يوفون أجورهم بغير حساب، أي لا يحاسبون في الآخرة، كما يحاسب غيرهم

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.claim: Others suggest verses 10 and 23 were also revealed during the Madinan period.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.anchor: Others suggest that vv. 10 and 23 were also revealed during the Madinan period

THALABI:v8p224/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p224/r10.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p224/r10.claim: Muqatil interprets the good promised to those who do good in this life as Paradise.
THALABI:v8p224/r10.anchor: أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة يعني الجنة

THALABI:v8p224/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p224/r11.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p224/r11.claim: Al-Suddi interprets that good as well-being and health.

THALABI:v8p224/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p224/r12.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p224/r12.claim: Mujahid understands God's spacious earth as a command to migrate and leave idol worship.
THALABI:v8p224/r12.anchor: وأرض الله واسعة فهاجروا فيها واعتزلوا الأوثان، قاله مجاهد

THALABI:v8p224/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p224/r13.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p224/r13.claim: Muqatil says the spacious earth refers to the Garden.

THALABI:v8p225/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p225/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p225/r1.claim: Qatada says the patient receive their reward without any measure or scales.
THALABI:v8p225/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: لا والله ما هنالك مكيال ولا ميزان

THALABI:v8p225/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p225/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p225/r2.claim: A report from Anas says worshippers receive measured rewards, whereas the afflicted receive reward poured out without reckoning, so the healthy will envy their merit.
THALABI:v8p225/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «تنصب الموازين يوم القيامة

THALABI:v8p225/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p225/r3.speaker: الحسن بن علي
THALABI:v8p225/r3.claim: Hasan ibn Ali recounts the Prophet's advice to fulfill obligations and be content, and that sufferers receive unmeasured reward beneath a tree of tribulation.
THALABI:v8p225/r3.anchor: سمعت جدي رسول الله يقول: «يا بني أد الفرائض

THALABI:v8p225/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p225/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p225/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet urges patience through harm and hardship, saying only the patient attain victory in the Resurrection.
THALABI:v8p225/r4.anchor: من سره أن يلحق بذوي الألباب والعقول فليصبر على الأذى والمكاره

THALABI:v8p226/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p226/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p226/r1.claim: A report from Abu Dharr says impatience leads its bearer toward Hell, while only the patient attain success, as confirmed by 13:24.
THALABI:v8p226/r1.anchor: ومن جزع صيره جزعه إلى النار، وما نال الفوز

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r4.claim: Verses 9–21 console oppressed monotheists: remain steadfast, migrate if necessary because God's land is spacious, and expect abundant reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r4.anchor: If it becomes difficult for them to live in this land, then the land of God is spacious enough for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r4.claim: Oppressed Muslims are urged to persevere in monotheism, assured of abundant reward, and told they may migrate because God's earth is vast.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r4.anchor: if it becomes difficult for them to live in their land, then they should rest assured that vast is God’s earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r2.claim: The persecuted poor Muslims are told to fear God, unlike polytheists who make divine justice and recompense meaningless through invented intercession; piety earns a great hereafter reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r2.anchor: After expressing lack of hope in the attitude of the Quraysh, assurance is sounded to the poor Muslims

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r3.claim: The promise that God’s earth is vast urges Muslims to endure persecution and, if worship becomes impossible in Makkah, move to a land where they can worship safely.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r3.anchor: If it is not possible for them to practice their religion in this city, then the Almighty will guide them to another land

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r4.claim: The sūrah’s setting is a period when Quraysh pressure made Muslims contemplate their future in Makkah; God reassured them that another land would receive them if expelled.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p535/r4.anchor: It is evident from this verse that this sūrah was revealed in that period of conflict between the proponents of good and evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r1.claim: The promise of reward without measure assures God’s servants that patient endurance of hardship will bring a reward beyond what they can imagine.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r1.anchor: servants of God who persevere in these trials will be blessed with a reward well beyond their hope and imagination

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r2.claim: The command that God’s earth is vast echoes the same instruction in Sūrah al-‘Ankabūt: adhere to God’s worship wherever you are.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p536/r2.anchor: this very context in Sūrah ‘Ankabūt in the following words

BURSEVI:v8p63/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63/r1.claim: “My servants” tells the believers to repeat these words exactly; the divine possessive address honors them, with the ياء omitted because the preceding kasra suffices.
BURSEVI:v8p63/r1.anchor: قل لهم قولي هذا بعينه وفيه تشريف لهم بإضافتهم إلى ضمير الجلالة

BURSEVI:v8p63/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63/r2.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p63/r2.claim: The address is to people who aligned themselves with the Real and preferred God's pleasure to the ego's desire, thereby attaining true servanthood and the title “My servants.”
BURSEVI:v8p63/r2.anchor: اين خطاب يا قومي است كه مراد نفس خويش بموافقت حق بدادند

BURSEVI:v8p63/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever despises his self for God's sake will be protected by God from the punishment of Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v8p63/r3.anchor: ومصطفى عليه السلام كفت "من مقت نفسه في ذات الله آمنه الله

BURSEVI:v8p63/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63/r4.speaker: أبو يزيد
BURSEVI:v8p63/r4.claim: Abu Yazid says that if asked to choose at the resurrection, he would ask to be thrown into Hell so he could present his self there, having suffered from it in worldly life.
BURSEVI:v8p63/r4.anchor: وأبو يزيد بسطامى قدس سره ميكويد اكر فرادى قيامت مرا كويند

BURSEVI:v8p63/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63/r5.claim: The most elect servants are freed from servitude to everything besides God, including this world and the next; they believe in God through longing and love as seekers.
BURSEVI:v8p63/r5.anchor: إن أخص الخواص هم العباد الذين خلصوا من عبودية الغير

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r1.claim: Ittaqu rabbakum can mean remain firm in piety, fear God's punishment through obedience and avoidance of sin, or use God as protection from everything besides Him to escape separation and attain union and the joy of His beauty.
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r1.anchor: اثبتوا على تقوى ربكم ، لأن الإيمان حصول التقوى

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r2.claim: Those who do good in this world perform righteous acts sincerely; the chief good deed is the testimony of faith.
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r2.anchor: عملوا الأعمال الحسنة في هذه الدنيا على وجه الإخلاص

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r3.claim: Grammatically, حسنة is the subject, للذين its predicate, and فى هذه الدنيا modifies أحسنوا.

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r4.claim: The promise alludes to the world as a farm for the next life: the great reward is Paradise and vision of God, whose reality is beyond knowing.

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r5.claim: Ihsan is to worship as though seeing God, knowing that He sees you; the true doer of good witnesses God, so other things disappear and sincerity is complete, while one attached to other-than-God risks shirk and ostentation.
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r5.anchor: الإحسان أن تعبد الله ، كأنك تراه

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r6.claim: A bad deed cannot earn a good reward.
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r6.anchor: ومن كان عمله قبيحا لم يكن جزاؤه حسنا

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r7.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r7.claim: The verse points to people who do good in seeking God and ask no good from anyone else; their good is finding God, which is deposited within sincere seeking.

BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r8.speaker: الخجندي
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r8.claim: His poem says to strive for the key to the treasure of existence, since the desired jewel cannot be found without seeking, and the lovers' end is blessed.
BURSEVI:v8p63#2/r8.anchor: حسن الوجدان مودع في حسن الطلب : قال الخجندي :

BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r1.claim: Those unable to maintain piety and excellence in their homeland should migrate where they can; prophets and righteous people set the precedent, and there is no excuse for neglect.
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r1.anchor: فليهاجر إلى حيث يتمكن فيه من ذلك

BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r2.claim: The verse urges migration from a place where sins are openly practiced.
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r2.anchor: حث على الهجرة من البلد الذي يظهر فيه المعاصي

BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r3.claim: A report promises Paradise to one who leaves one land for another to protect religion; the author distinguishes religious flight from worldly motives, especially when the destination is more sinful.
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r3.anchor: إن من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض وجبت له الجنة

BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r4.claim: Inwardly, God’s presence has no limit: visions and unveilings never mean the seeker has reached the highest aim, since nearness and arrival have no endpoint; Rumi likewise urges continuing beyond each threshold.
BURSEVI:v8p63#3/r4.anchor: يشير إلى حضرة جلاله أنه لا نهاية لها فلا يغتر طالب بما يفتح عليه من أبواب المشاهدات والمكاشفات

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r1.claim: The patient keep their religion and its limits through persecution and suffering, including the pain of leaving family and homeland; their reward corresponds to what they endured and is beyond counting.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r1.anchor: الذين صبروا على دينهم ، فلم يتركوه للأذى

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r2.claim: He explains divine full recompense with the lexicon’s sense of giving or taking something in full.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r2.anchor: توفية الشيء بذله وافيا كاملا واستيفاؤه تناوله وافيا

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r3.claim: A report says scales are set for prayer, charity, and pilgrimage, but not for the afflicted: their reward is poured out until the healthy wish they had been cut with shears for such merit.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r3.anchor: أنه تنصب الموازين يوم القيامة لأهل الصلاة والصدقة والحج

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r4.speaker: سفيان
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r4.claim: Sufyan relates that the Prophet first sought more than tenfold reward for his community, then more than the seven-hundredfold described in 2:261, until this verse came and he stopped asking.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r4.anchor: قال سفيان : لما نزل {من جآء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها}

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r5.claim: The Prophet says prophets are tested most, followed by those most like them; the trial matches religious firmness and continues until the person walks free of sin.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r5.anchor: قال : "الأنبياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل يبتلى الرجل على حسب دينه"

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r6.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r6.claim: A person unable to attain a divinely assigned rank through deeds may be tried in body, wealth, or child; patience through the trial brings that rank.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r6.anchor: إن العبد إذا سبقت له من الله منزلة لم يبلغها بعمله ابتلاه الله في جسده

BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r7.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r7.claim: The greatest reward accompanies the greatest trial; God tests those He loves, and acceptance earns His pleasure while resentment earns His displeasure.
BURSEVI:v8p63#4/r7.anchor: وإن أعظم الجزاء مع عظم البلاء ، وإن الله عز وجل إذا أحب قوما ابتلاهم

BURSEVI:v8p64/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r1.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r1.claim: Al-Baqli describes the people through four qualities: faith, God-consciousness, excellence, and patience.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r1.anchor: وصف الله القوم بأربع خصال : بالإيمان والتقوى والإحسان والصبر

BURSEVI:v8p64/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r2.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r2.claim: Their faith is direct knowledge of God and His attributes through God, without inference from created events.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r2.anchor: فأما إيمانهم فهو المعرفة بذاته وصفاته من غير استدلال بالحدثان

BURSEVI:v8p64/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r3.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r3.claim: Their piety strips the self of attachment to created existence until they stand without a veil from God.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r3.anchor: تقواهم فتجريدهم أنفسهم عن الكون حتى قاموا بلا احتجاب عنه

BURSEVI:v8p64/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r4.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r4.claim: Their excellence is perceiving divine vision in hearts and spirits through the unveiling of divine beauty; their patience is steadfastness in states while concealing the complete unveiling.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r4.anchor: وأما إحسانهم فإدراكهم رؤيته تعالى بقلوبهم وأرواحهم بنعت كشف جماله

BURSEVI:v8p64/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r5.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r5.claim: True patience does not claim permanence after attaining it. Inwardly, God’s spacious earth is the heart, expanded by the Real.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r5.anchor: وحقيقة الصبر أن لا يدعي الديمومة بعد الاتصاف بها

BURSEVI:v8p64/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r6.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r6.claim: The gnostic receives a worldly reward of extraordinary inspirations and arrivals, and an afterlife reward of immersion in eternity, annihilation in the Essence, and abiding in the attributes.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r6.anchor: فإذا كان العارف بهذه الأوصاف ، فله أجران : أجر الدنيا

BURSEVI:v8p64/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r7.speaker: الحارث المحاسبي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r7.claim: Al-Harith al-Muhasibi defines patience as exposing oneself to the arrows of affliction.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r7.anchor: قال الحارث المحاسبي : الصبر التهدف لسهام البلاء

BURSEVI:v8p64/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r8.speaker: طاهر المقدسي
BURSEVI:v8p64/r8.claim: Tahir al-Maqdisi distinguishes patience from, for, upon, and within God; the least difficult is patience in obeying God, for which this verse promises reward.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r8.anchor: وقال طاهر المقدسي : الصبر على وجوه صبر منه وصبر له وصبر عليه

BURSEVI:v8p64/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p64/r9.speaker: يوسف بن الحسين
BURSEVI:v8p64/r9.claim: Yusuf ibn al-Husayn says the patient person does not merely endure calamity while showing aversion, but delights in patience until reaching contentment.
BURSEVI:v8p64/r9.anchor: وقال يوسف بن الحسين : ليس بصابر من يتجرع المصيبة ويبدي فيها الكراهة

QASHANI:39:10-12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:10-12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:10-12/r1.claim: The cared-for believers efface their attributes; those who do good take on divine attributes and worship through witnessing, whose goodness is seeing the enduring Face and noble Beauty.
QASHANI:39:10-12/r1.anchor: اتصفوا بالصفات الإلهية فعبدوه على المشاهدة

QASHANI:39:10-12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:10-12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:10-12/r2.claim: God's spacious earth is the contented self, submitted to Him and accepting His light; certainty frees it from habits and anything but truth.
QASHANI:39:10-12/r2.anchor: أي: النفس المطمئنة المخصوصة بالله لانقيادها له وقبولها لنوره واطمئنانها إليه

QASHANI:39:10-12/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:10-12/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:10-12/r3.claim: The patient travel with God in effacement of attributes and acts; their reward is gardens of attributes without measure, infinite unlike finite material effects.
QASHANI:39:10-12/r3.anchor: الذين صبروا مع الله في فناء صفاتهم وأفعالهم وسلوكهم فيه وسيرهم في منازل النفس الواسعة باليقين

QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r10.claim: Those who do good through obedience receive good in this world; excellence means performing all that one can.
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r10.anchor: بأداء الطاعات ، ( والإحسان هو الإتيان بجيمع وجوه الإمكان )

QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r11.claim: Do not use enemy persecution as an excuse to leave worship: God’s earth is wide, so move somewhere that allows worship to continue.
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r11.anchor: فأرض الله واسعة ، فاخرجوا منها إلى موضع آخر تتم لكم فيه عبادتكم

QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r12.claim: Patience means restraining the self from what it dislikes; it is also drinking the cups of decree without resistance or frowning, or exposing oneself to the arrows of trial.
QUSHAYRI:v3p113/r12.anchor: والصبر حبس النفس على ما تكرهه

SULAMI:v2p193#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r1.speaker: الحارث المحاسبي
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r1.claim: Patience exposes oneself to the arrows of affliction.
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r1.anchor: قال حارث المحاسبي : الصبر التهدف بسهام البلاء

SULAMI:v2p193#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r2.claim: Patience restrains limbs and movements from disobedience while seeking the reward God promises to the patient.
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - : الصبر ذم الجوارح والحركات عن جميع المخالفات

SULAMI:v2p193#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r3.speaker: طاهر المقدسي
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r3.claim: Patience may be from God, for God, upon God, or in God; the easiest is patience with His commands and prohibitions, for which He promises reward.
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r3.anchor: قال طاهر المقدسي : الصبر على وجوه : صبر منه وصبر له وصبر عليه

SULAMI:v2p193#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r4.claim: Patience is carrying burdens until the days of hardship end.
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r4.anchor: سئل الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - عن الصبر ؟ فقال : حمل المؤن حتى تنقضي أيام المكروه

SULAMI:v2p193#5/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r5.speaker: الخواص
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r5.claim: Most people falsely claim to bear patience's burdens because they keep seeking worldly means and rely on them as if they were lords.
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r5.anchor: وقال الخواص : كذب اكثر الخلق في حمل اثقال الصبر بما لحوا إلى الطلب والأسباب

SULAMI:v2p193#5/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r6.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r6.claim: His poem portrays a lover's traces of tears and cries for patience as patience itself calls for help.
SULAMI:v2p193#5/r6.anchor: وانشد لذي النون : عبدات خططن في الخد سطرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r3.claim: After praising believers who worship at difficult hours, fear and hope in God, and learn, the Prophet is told to address them to strengthen their resolve; the implied command is قل للمؤمنين.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r3.anchor: أتبع ذلك بأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالإقبال على خطابهم للاستزادة من ثباتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r4.claim: The command to say, the divine-servant address, and its attribution to God mark the message as important and place believers in the elevated position of being directly addressed by God; the vocative yā is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p351/r4.anchor: وابتداء الكلام بالأمر بالقول للوجه الذي تقدم في نظيره آنفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r1.claim: All ten readers omit the possessive yā in يا عباد at pause and in liaison; this differs from 39:53 and the consonantal text omits it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r1.anchor: وقرأه العشرة { ياعباد بدون ياء في الوصل والوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya's attribution of a reading with possessive yā to most readers confuses this verse with 39:53, where readings differ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r2.anchor: وما وقع في ( تفسير ابن عطية ) من قوله : وقرأ جمهور القراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r3.claim: The command to remain God-conscious addresses people already pious and implies hardship could weaken their observance; it prepares them for migration for safety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r3.anchor: والأمر بالتقوى مراد به الدوام على المأمور به لأنهم متقون من قبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r4.claim: The phrase those who believe implies their faith is established despite pressure that may force an outward show of disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r4.anchor: وفي استحضارهم بالموصول وصلته إيماء إلى أن تقرر إيمانهم مما يقتضي التقوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r5.claim: The promise of worldly goodness explains why pious believers are addressed and prepares for the assurance of broad safe lands; it may also be the reason for the command to fear God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p352/r5.anchor: وجملة { للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة } وما عطف عليها استئناف بياني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r1.claim: Those who do good are the God-fearing believers described in 39:9; their traits match the Prophetic definition of ihsan as worshipping as though seeing God, and the relative phrase includes anyone with that quality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r1.anchor: والمراد بالذين أحسنوا : الذين اتقوا الله وهم المؤمنون الموصوفون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r2.claim: The implied invitation is to fear God and become doers of good, who receive great goodness; fronting the prepositional phrase gives special attention to those receiving God's kindness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r2.anchor: وذلك في معنى : اتقوا ربكم لتكونوا محسنين فإن للذين أحسنوا حسنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r3.claim: حسنة means a good condition, with its noun omitted after the adjective, as in 2:201; the corresponding inverse uses the same transfer in 42:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r3.anchor: والمراد بالحسنة الحالة الحسنة ، واستغني بالوصف عن الموصوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r4.claim: Positioning في هذه الدنيا between the doers of good and their reward permits multiple meanings and is a Quranic stylistic feature; it can mark worldly recompense in a passage reassuring persecuted believers and urging migration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r4.anchor: وتوسيط قوله : { في هذه الدنيا } بين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the good condition in this world as health and well-being.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r5.anchor: قال السدي : الحسنة في الدنيا الصحة والعافية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r6.claim: Alternatively, في الدنيا can modify أحسنوا, urging believers to perform good deeds in earthly life before opportunity passes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p353/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قوله : ( في الدنيا ) متعلقا بفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r1.claim: The indefinite حسنَة is magnified; this may be intrinsic for the afterlife or qualitative for worldly good, and the demonstrative identifies its referent, as in the prayer of 2:201.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r1.anchor: وتنوين { حسنة } للتعظيم وهو بالنسبة لحسنة الآخرة للتعظيم الذاتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r2.claim: The wording parallels the promise in 16:30, whose further statement that the Hereafter is better supplies what is settled but unstated here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم نظير هذه الآية في سورة النحل قوله تعالى : { وقيل للذين اتقوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r3.claim: Saying God's earth is vast indirectly urges migration from religious persecution; its factual obviousness signals this implied purpose, like a proverb, and 4:97 states it explicitly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r3.anchor: عطف المقصود على التوطئة . وهو خبر مستعمل في التعريض بالحث على الهجرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the address to believers refers to Jaafar ibn Abi Talib and his companions who migrated to Abyssinia; the allusion gently eases the pain of leaving home.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى : { قل يا عباد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r5.claim: The migration promised a good outcome away from Meccan unbelief, as 4:97 explicitly asks whether God's earth was wide enough to migrate through.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p354/r5.anchor: وقد وقع التصريح بما كني عنه هنا في قوله تعالى : { قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r1.claim: The closing promise of immeasurable reward for the patient is a conclusion to the goodness and migration promise, since leaving home and traveling are hardships; it reassures migrants of their reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r1.anchor: وموقع جملة { إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب } موقع التذييل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r2.claim: Patience is composure when pain and calamity arrive; the plural covers everyone enduring the duties, commands, and prohibitions, with reward varying by degree.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r2.anchor: والصبر : سكون النفس عند حلول الآلام والمصائب بأن لا تضجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r3.claim: Tawfiya means giving in full, and Quranic usage makes ajr the reward of the Hereafter; reward without account figuratively signals abundance beyond enumeration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r3.anchor: والتوفية : إعطاء الشيء وافيا ، أي تاما . والأجر : الثواب في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r4.claim: Calling it their reward comforts believers that they earned it, although all remains God's grace; the wording parallels 84:25.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r4.anchor: وفي ذكر التوفية وإضافة الأجر إلى ضميرهم تأنيس لهم بأنهم استحقوا ذلك لا منة عليهم فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r5.claim: إنما restricts the reward to being without account, correcting the belief that recompense merely matches the measure of one's hardship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r6.claim: The Abyssinian migration occurred in year five before the Medina migration after persecution; the Prophet cited a just king, and 83 men and 19 women went, excluding children.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r6.anchor: والهجرة إلى الحبشة كانت سنة خمس قبل الهجرة إلى المدينة . وكان سببها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r7.claim: Abu Bakr asked leave to migrate, set out for Abyssinia, but Ibn al-Dughunna stopped him and took him under protection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p355/r7.anchor: وقد كان أبو بكر الصديق استأذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الهجرة فأذن له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p356/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p356/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p356/r1.claim: God kept the Prophet in Mecca to establish Islam at its birthplace, while allowing persecuted believers to leave; after Medina embraced Islam and migration served expansion, He prepared the Prophet's move through providence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p356/r1.anchor: ولما تعلقت إرادة الله تعالى بنشر الإسلام في مكة بين العرب لحكمة اقتضت ذلك

NAHHAS:v4p7/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r1.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p7/r1.claim: Taqwa here is interpreted as avoiding God’s disobedience; the ta in اتقوا is said to replace wāw.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r1.anchor: قيل معناه اتقوا معاصيه والتاء مبدلة من واو

NAHHAS:v4p7/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p7/r2.claim: One parse places في هذه الدنيا inside the relative clause, making the promised good belong to the Hereafter.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون في الدنيا داخلا في الصلة أي لهم حسنة في الآخرة

NAHHAS:v4p7/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is outside the relative clause, so the good is in this world: God’s friendship, praise, and giving the doers good names.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r3.anchor: فالمعنى للذين أحسنوا حسنة في الدنيا فالحسنة التي لهم في هذه الدنيا موالاة الله

NAHHAS:v4p7/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r4.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p7/r4.claim: One interpretation of God’s spacious earth is that it means the Garden.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r4.anchor: ( وأرض الله واسعة ) في معناه قولان أحدهما أنه يراد بها أرض الجنة

NAHHAS:v4p7/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r5.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p7/r5.claim: Alternatively, the earth is literally spacious, so believers should migrate and not remain among those who sin.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r5.anchor: والآخر أن معناه أن أرض الله واسعة فهاجروا فيها ولا تقيموا مع من يعمل بالمعاصي

NAHHAS:v4p7/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p7/r6.claim: The praiseworthy patient person is one who restrains himself from sins; enduring a sin is expressed as being patient with something.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r6.anchor: صابر يمدح به إنما هو لمن صبر عن المعاصي فإن أردت أنه صابر على المعصية

NAHHAS:v4p7/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r7.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p7/r7.claim: بغير حساب can mean without measure.

NAHHAS:v4p7/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r8.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p7/r8.claim: It can mean reward beyond calculation, since reward matching deeds would be measured against them.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r8.anchor: وقيل يراد على الثواب أنه لو أعطي بقدر ما عمل لكان بحساب

NAHHAS:v4p7/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r9.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p7/r9.claim: It can also mean no subsequent accounting, follow-up, or demand as with worldly favors.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r9.anchor: وقيل معنى بغير حساب بغير متابعة ولا مطالبة كما تقع المطالبة بنعم الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r7.claim: Most read yā ʿibādi with an open yāʾ; Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and al-Aʿmash also read it silent, and several readers drop the yāʾ in connected reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r7.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء: «قل يا عبادي» بفتح الياء.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r8.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about Jaʿfar b. Abi Talib and his companions when they planned to migrate to Abyssinia.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r8.anchor: ويروى أن هذه الآية نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وأصحابه حين عزموا على الهجرة إلى أرض الحبشة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r9.claim: Muqatil takes the good promised to those who do good in this world as a good reward in the Hereafter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r9.anchor: في الآخرة وهي الجنة والنعيم، قاله مقاتل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r10.claim: Al-Suddi instead takes the promised good as an outcome, victory, or God's support in this world; the author prefers the Hereafter interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r10.anchor: قاله السدي. وكان قياس قوله أن يكون في هذه الدنيا متأخرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r11.claim: God's spacious earth means neighboring lands implied by the migration story; taking it as Paradise is an unsupported assertion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523/r11.anchor: وأرض الله يريد بها البلاد المجاورة التي تقتضيها القصة التي في الكلام فيها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.claim: The promise of reward without measure covers patience through hardship, emigration, support of the faith, and every act of obedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.anchor: ثم وعد تعالى على الصبر على المكاره والخروج عن الوطن ونصرة الدين وجميع الطاعات: بأن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.claim: One interpretation says the patient receive their reward without being called to account for its pleasures or pursued for sins, identifying them with a Prophetic group who enter Paradise without reckoning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أن الصابر يوفى أجره ثم لا يحاسب عن نعيم ولا يتابع بذنوب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.claim: The hadith identifies seventy thousand from the Prophet's community who enter Paradise without reckoning as those who avoid omens, cauterization, and seeking incantations, and rely on God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.anchor: هم الذين لا يتطيرون ولا يكتوون ولا يسترقون وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.claim: The majority take the phrase to mean the patient are paid without limit or enumeration, a metaphor for uncountable abundance; Qatada says there is no measure or scale.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى الثاني: أن أجور الصابرين توفى بغير حصر ولا عد، بل جزافا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.claim: Qatada stresses that there is no measure or scale for the reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.anchor: حتى قال قتادة: ليس ثم والله مكيال ولا ميزان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.claim: A report says that after 2:261, the Prophet prayed for more reward for his community; after 2:245 and then this verse, he said he was satisfied.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.anchor: وفي بعض الحديث أنه لما نزلت: والله يضاعف لمن يشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r1.claim: The promise of a good reward for those who do good in this world was explained earlier under 16:30.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r2.claim: “God’s earth is spacious” either urges believers to migrate from Mecca to a place of safety or describes the expanse of Paradise as an inducement.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r2.anchor: قولان أحدهما أنه حث لهم على الهجرة من مكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r3.claim: Those who patiently endure for God what befalls them receive a gift too vast to count or encompass, beyond the measure of their deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p168/r3.anchor: الذين صبروا لأجل الله تعالى على مانالهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.claim: Believers are commanded to persist in obedience and piety; those who do good receive goodness in this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r1.anchor: آمرا عباده المؤمنين بالاستمرار على طاعته وتقواه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r2.claim: The earth is wide, so emigrate, strive, and keep away from idols.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.claim: When summoned to sin, flee elsewhere; Ata cites the instruction to migrate when the earth is wide.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r3.anchor: إذا دعيتم إلى المعصية فاهربوا، ثم قرأ: {ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.speaker: الأوزاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.claim: The patient’s reward is not weighed or measured but poured out abundantly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r4.anchor: ليس يوزن لهم ولا يكال (1) ، إنما يغرف لهم غرفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says their deeds’ reward is never counted but increased beyond it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r5.anchor: لا يحسب عليهم ثواب عملهم قط، ولكن يزادون (2) على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the patient’s unlimited recompense is in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p89#2/r6.anchor: إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} يعني: في الجنة

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r2.claim: Those who do good in this world receive a good reward in the afterlife: abiding in Paradise.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r2.anchor: من أحسن العمل في الدنيا فله مثوبة حسنة في الآخرة

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r3.claim: Iḥsān can mean generosity toward others and inviting them to religion, or doing what is good by obeying God's commands.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r3.anchor: إحسان إلى الغير بالإنعام عليه والدعاء إلى الدين

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r4.claim: The worldly good may be praise and kind words, while the afterlife good is abundant reward; alternatives define it as goodness (Muqātil) or health and well-being (al-Suddī).
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r4.anchor: حسنة في الدنيا بالثناء والمدح والقول الجميل

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r5.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r5.claim: God's spacious earth means the worldly earth, so believers should migrate from the land of polytheism.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r5.anchor: الدنيا واسعة، فتهاجروا عن دار الشرك، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r6.speaker: مقاتل وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes the spacious land as Paradise, to be sought through righteous deeds; another encourages moving to the many fruitful lands promised to them.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r6.anchor: أرض الجنة واسعة فاطلبوها بالأعمال الصالحة، عن مقاتل، وأبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r7.claim: Patience may mean enduring migration and exile, obeying and avoiding sin, or bearing afflictions and trials.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r7.anchor: قيل: على الهجرة وترك الوطن والإقامة بالغربة، وقيل: على الطاعة وعن المعصية

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r8.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r8.claim: The patient receive reward beyond the measure of their deeds.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r8.anchor: لأنه يعطي أكثر من مقادير الأعمال، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r9.claim: Alternatively, “without reckoning” means without constriction, since a measured reward would be restricted.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r9.anchor: وقيل: لا [تضييق] فيه؛ لأن ما يعطى بحساب يتضيق، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r10.claim: Qatādah emphatically says there is no measuring vessel or scale there.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r10.anchor: قال قتادة: لا، والله ما هناك مكيال، ولا ميزان

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r11.claim: The verse implies complete divine power and knowledge, perception without instruments, that God does not will evil or punish without guilt, and encouragement of knowledge, migration, and obedience.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r11.anchor: تدل الآية على أحكام: منها: كمال قدرته وعلمه. وأنه مدرك لا بآلة

JISHUMI:v8p6045/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r1.claim: The statements that God does not approve disbelief for His servants, accepts gratitude, and does not let one soul bear another's burden refute attribution of wrongful conduct to Him.

JISHUMI:v8p6045/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r3.claim: References to the devout person, hope for mercy, reflection, idolaters, misleading others, and fearing God refute the claim that human acts are created in people by God.
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r3.anchor: قوله: (أمن هو قانت)، وقوله: (ويرجو رحمة ربه)، وقوله: (إنما يتذكر)

JISHUMI:v8p6045/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r6.claim: The good-doer is repaid with good; this depends on the doctrine that people act and God rewards the good-doer for good and the evildoer for evil.
JISHUMI:v8p6045/r6.anchor: أن المحسن يجازى بالإحسان، وجميع ذلك إنما يصح على مذهب العدل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r1.claim: He attaches fi hadhihi al-dunya to ahsanu, meaning those who do good in this world receive an indescribably good reward in the afterlife, namely Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r1.anchor: متعلق بأحسنوا لا بحسنة ، معناه : الذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا فلهم حسنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r2.speaker: السدي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r2.claim: Al-Suddi attaches the phrase to hasanah and interprets the worldly good as health and well-being.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r2.anchor: وقد علقه السدي بحسنة ، ففسر بحسنة بالصحة والعافية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r3.claim: Although the phrase cannot be an adjective before hasanah, when it precedes it can specify where the good is located; the order does not prevent the attachment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p119/r3.anchor: هو صفة لها إذا تأخر فإذا تقدم كان بيانا لمكانها فلم يخل التقدم بالتعلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r1.claim: The promised good may be Paradise in the Hereafter, or a good granted in this world in addition to the reward of the Hereafter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r1.anchor: للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة في الآخرة , وهي الجنة . الثاني : للذين أحسنوا في الدنيا حسنة في الدنيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r2.claim: He identifies the worldly good as safety and health.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r3.claim: He identifies it as whatever good God provides in worldly life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r3.anchor: ما رزقهم الله من خير الدنيا , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r4.claim: He reads the good as obedience granted in this world and Paradise in the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r4.anchor: ما أعطاهم من طاعته في الدنيا وجنته في الآخرة , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r5.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r5.claim: He identifies the good as victory and spoils.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r6.claim: A further possibility is praise in this world and recompense in the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r6.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا : إن الحسنة في الدنيا الثناء وفي الآخرة الجزاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r7.claim: He takes the spacious earth as the expanse of Paradise, offered to encourage believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r7.anchor: أرض الجنة رغبهم في سعتها , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r8.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r8.claim: He understands it as the land of migration.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r9.claim: He suggests spacious land means abundant provision from the earth, since the wording presents it as a favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r9.anchor: أن يريد بسعة الأرض سعة الرزق لأنه يرزقهم من الأرض فيكون معناه . ورزق الله واسع , وهو أشبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r10.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r10.claim: Reward without reckoning means no reproach or follow-up claim is placed on them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r10.anchor: بغير من عليهم ولا متابعة , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r11.claim: They receive more than the amount calculated from their deeds alone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r11.anchor: لا يحسب لهم ثواب عملهم فقط ولكن يزدادون على ذلك , قاله ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r12.claim: It may mean a gift that is not measured but given freely, or a wide reward without restriction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r12.anchor: لا يعطونه مقدرا لكن جزافا . الرابع : واسعا بغير تضييق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r13.claim: A rajaz verse uses the phrase for generous, unmeasured watering; Ali compares patient people's reward to handfuls poured out rather than weighed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p118/r13.anchor: وحكي عن علي كرم الله وجهه قال : كل أجر يكال كيلا ويوزن وزنا إلا أجر الصابرين فإنه يحثى حثوا

MUJAHID:v2p556#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p556#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p556#2/r1.claim: The command that God's earth is vast means migrate and withdraw from worship of idols.
MUJAHID:v2p556#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وأرض الله واسعة ﴾ يقول فهاجروا واعتزلوا عبادة الأوثان

MUQATIL:39:8-10/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:8-10/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:8-10/r3.claim: Believers should fear God; good-doers receive Paradise, and God’s wide earth means Medina. Those patient in emigration receive Paradise and provisions without measure.
MUQATIL:39:8-10/r3.anchor: { وأرض الله واسعة } يعنى المدينة { إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم } يعنى جزاءهم الجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r1.speaker: الأكثر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r1.claim: Most readers omit the yāʾ in يا عباد.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا ﴾ بلا ياء عند الاكثر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r2.claim: God-consciousness means obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ اتقوا ربكم ﴾ بامتثال اوامره واجتناب نواهيه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.claim: Those who obey God in this life receive an indescribably good reward in the afterlife, entry into Paradise; في belongs to أحسنوا, not حسنة.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.anchor: أى أطاعوا الله فى الدنيا وفى يتعلق بأحسنوا لا بحسنة معناه الذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا فلهم حسنة في الآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.speaker: السدي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī attaches في to حسنة and interprets the good as health and well-being.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.anchor: وقد علقه السدى بحسنة ففسر الحسنة بالصحة والعافية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.claim: The earth's breadth removes any excuse for neglecting virtue at home: migrate to another land, following prophets and righteous people, and increase in good deeds and obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ وأرض الله واسعة ﴾ أى لا عذر للمفرطين فى الاحسان ألبته حتى ان اعتلوا بأنهم لا يتمكنون فى أوطانهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.claim: The patient endure leaving homes and kin, hardships, and trials for obedience and added good works; their reward exceeds calculation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.anchor: على مفارقة أوطانهم وعشائرهم وعلى غيرها من تجرع الغصص واحتمال البلايا فى طاعة الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says their reward is beyond what a calculator can comprehend or know; this phrase is circumstantial description of the reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p49#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما لا يهتدى إليه حساب الحساب ولا يعرف وهو حال من الأجر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r1.claim: The address tells believers to fear their Lord by avoiding disobedience; the tāʾ in ittaqū substitutes for wāw.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r1.anchor: أي اتقوا معاصيه والتاء مبدلة من واو

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the address particularly concerns Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib and companions who emigrated with him to Abyssinia.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد جعفر بن أبي طالب والذين خرجوا معه إلى الحبشة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r3.claim: The first “good” means obedience in this life and the second means Paradise's reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r3.anchor: يعني بالحسنة الأولى الطاعة وبالثانية الثواب في الجنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r4.claim: Another view promises worldly good in addition to the afterlife reward, including health, safety, victory, and booty.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى للذين أحسنوا في الدنيا حسنة في الدنيا، يكون ذلك زيادة على ثواب الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r5.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r5.claim: Al-Qushayri prefers the afterlife-reward reading because unbelievers also receive worldly blessings.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r5.anchor: قال القشيري: والأول أصح لأن الكافر قد نال نعم الدنيا.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r6.claim: The author responds that believers also enjoy worldly blessings and receive Paradise when they are grateful.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r6.anchor: قلت: وينالها معه المؤمن ويزاد الجنة إذا شكر تلك النعم.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r7.claim: “Good” may also mean a good reputation in this life, with recompense in the next.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r7.anchor: وقد تكون الحسنة في الدنيا الثناء الحسن، وفي الآخرة الجزاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r8.claim: One alternative means the spacious land of Paradise, supported by 3:133 and 39:74.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r8.anchor: وقيل: المراد أرض الجنة رغبهم في سعتها وسعة نعيمها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r9.claim: The apparent meaning is a command to emigrate away from sinful company; the author says it means leaving Mecca for a safe place.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r9.anchor: والأول أظهر فهو أمر بالهجرة. أي ارحلوا من مكة إلى حيث تأمنوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r10.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r10.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests spaciousness means abundant provision from the earth; the author finds this plausible and says it supports moving to a cheaper land.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r10.anchor: الماوردي: يحتمل أن يريد بسعة الأرض سعة الرزق لأنه يرزقهم من الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r11.claim: On that reading, the verse supports moving from an expensive land to one where bread costs less, as Sufyan al-Thawri advised.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r11.anchor: قلت: فتكون الآية دليلا على الانتقال من الأرض الغالية، إلى الأرض الراخية

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r12.claim: “The patient” may mean fasters, based on God's saying that fasting belongs to Him and He rewards it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10/r12.anchor: و«الصابرون» هنا الصائمون دليله قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام مخبرا عن الله عز وجل:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r1.claim: A divine report says fasting belongs to God, who alone gives its reward.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r2.claim: Scholars say other deeds are weighed, but fasting is rewarded in handfuls and scoops; this is also related from ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r2.anchor: قال أهل العلم: كل أجر يكال كيلا ويوزن وزنا إلا الصوم فإنه يحثى حثوا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r3.speaker: مالك بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r3.claim: Malik identifies patience as endurance of life's calamities and griefs; whoever bears what befalls him and avoids prohibitions has unmeasured reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r3.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس في قوله: { إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب } قال: هو الصبر على فجائع الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r4.claim: Qatadah transmits from Anas that people tested by affliction receive reward without a scale or register, poured upon them, while ordinary deeds are weighed.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا والله ما هناك مكيال ولا ميزان، حدثني أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r5.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r5.claim: The report from Anas says those who enjoyed worldly well-being will wish their bodies had been cut apart when they see the afflicted people's reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r5.anchor: حتى يتمنى أهل العافية في الدنيا أن أجسادهم تقرض بالمقاريض

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r6.speaker: الحسين بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r6.claim: Al-Husayn ibn ʿAli transmits from his grandfather the Prophet that the afflicted in Paradise's tree of trial receive reward without measure.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r6.anchor: وعن الحسين بن علي رضي الله عنهما قال: سمعت جدي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r7.speaker: الحسين بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r7.claim: The Prophet's report concludes by reciting that the patient receive their reward without reckoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r7.anchor: ثم تلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب }.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r8.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas notes that ṣābir praises one who is patient against sin; endurance of a calamity is expressed as patience “on” it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:10#2/r8.anchor: وإذا أردت أنه صبر على المصيبة قلت صابر على كذا قاله النحاس.

SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r1.claim: في هذه الدنيا may attach to the preceding verb; حسنة has an omitted qualifier meaning great goodness, since an unqualified good deed is not the promised reward.
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق بالفعل قبله؛ وحذفت صفة " حسنة " ، إذ المعنى: حسنة عظيمة

SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r2.claim: Alternatively the phrase attaches to an omitted element as a circumstantial qualifier; it was an adjective of حسنة before being advanced.
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r2.anchor: وأن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنها حال من حسنة كانت صفة لها، فلما تقدمت بقيت حالا

SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r3.claim: بغير حساب is circumstantial for أجرهم or الصابرون, meaning the reward is unreckoned or the patient are not reckoned against.
SAMIN-DURR:39:10/r3.anchor: و " بغير حساب " حال: إما من " أجرهم " ، وإما من " الصابرون " أي: غير محاسب عليه، أو غير محاسبين

RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r1.claim: The command to believing servants to add God-consciousness to faith is evidence that faith remains alongside sin.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r1.anchor: والمراد أن الله تعالى أمر المؤمنين بأن يضموا إلى الإيمان التقوى ، وهذا من أول الدلائل على أن الإيمان يبقى مع المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r2.claim: The Qadi says believers are commanded to fear God so their faith and its reward are not nullified: avoiding major sins preserves reward, while committing them cancels it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r2.anchor: قال القاضي : أمرهم بالتقوى ليكلا يحبطوا إيمانهم ، لأن عند الاتقاء من الكبائر يسلم لهم الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r3.claim: Al-Razi answers that exhorting believers to fear God more strongly implies they remain believers even when they fail to do so; grave sin does not remove faith.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220/r3.anchor: لما أمر المؤمنين بالتقوى دل ذلك على أنه يبقى مؤمنا مع عدم التقوى

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r1.claim: If “in this world” modifies doing good, the verse promises every good-doer a magnificent afterlife reward, namely Paradise, whose perfection reason cannot encompass.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r1.anchor: في الآخرة ، وهي دخول الجنة ، والتنكير في قوله : { حسنة }

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r2.claim: If the phrase modifies “goodness,” the promise is worldly well-being; some identify it as health, safety, and sufficiency, which the Prophet describes as inexhaustible blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r2.anchor: وأما على التقدير الثاني : فمعناه الذين أحسنوا فلهم في هذه الدنيا حسنة

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic saying names security, health, and sufficiency as three blessings without end.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r3.anchor: ثلاثة ليس لها نهاية : الأمن والصحة والكفاية

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi prefers the afterlife reading: the indefinite “goodness” suggests majesty suited to the lasting afterlife, not transient worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r4.anchor: أن التنكير في قوله : { حسنة } يدل على النهاية والجلالة والرفعة

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r5.claim: The afterlife reading fits because reward for monotheism and good deeds comes there, while health, security, and sufficiency also reach unbelievers, often more fully.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r5.anchor: حاصلة للكفار ، وأيضا فحصولها للكافر أكثر وأتم من حصولها للمؤمن

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying calls worldly life a prison for the believer and a garden for the unbeliever.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r6.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( الدنيا سجن المؤمن وجنة الكافر )

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r7.claim: The verse’s restrictive force rules out worldly well-being, since worldly blessings are not exclusive to those who do good; it coherently describes afterlife reward.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r7.anchor: يفيد الحصر ، بمعنى أنه يفيد أن حسنة هذه الدنيا لا تحصل إلا للذين أحسنوا ، وهذا باطل

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r8.claim: One interpretation of “God’s earth is vast” says people have no excuse for failing to do good because of their homeland; they should move where worship is possible, as the prophets and righteous did.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r8.anchor: المراد أنه لا عذر ألبتة للمقصرين في الإحسان ، حتى إنهم إن اعتلوا بأوطانهم وبلادهم

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r9.claim: This reading encourages migration from Mecca to Medina and patience in leaving one’s homeland.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r9.anchor: والمقصود منه الترغيب في الهجرة من مكة إلى المدينة والصبر على مفارقة الوطن

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r10.claim: Abu Muslim says “God’s earth” means Paradise: the verse moves from piety to the good reward of eternal residence in the vast Garden.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : لا يمتنع أن يكون المراد من الأرض أرض الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r11.claim: Al-Razi prefers the first interpretation of the vast earth, since the following promise of immeasurable reward fits migration and patient endurance.
RAZI-FULL:v26p220#2/r11.anchor: والقول الأول عندي أولى ، لأن قوله : { إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب } لا يليق إلا بالأول

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r1.claim: The patient rewarded here are those who endured exile from homes and kin, bitter hardships, and afflictions in obedience to God.
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r1.anchor: المراد ههنا بالصابرين الذين صبروا على مفارقة أوطانهم وعشائرهم

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r2.claim: Calling the promised benefit an ajr does not imply that deeds entitle people to reward; it means reward according to God's promise.
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r2.anchor: فوجب حمل لفظ الأجر على كونه أجرا بحسب الوعد

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r3.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r3.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the patient receive what they deserve plus a gracious excess; the total is beyond reckoning.
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r3.anchor: المعنى أنهم يعطون ما يستحقون ويزدادون تفضلا فهو بغير حساب

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects al-Jubbāʾī's account: if only the due reward were given, that would still be reward, not gratuitous excess.

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r5.claim: One reading takes “without reckoning” to mean endless reward, since whatever can be counted is finite.
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r5.anchor: معناه بغير نهاية ، لأن كل شيء دخل تحت الحساب فهو متناه

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r6.claim: Another reading is reward beyond human conception: the people of Paradise find what they see greater than they imagined, as the Prophetic report says.
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r6.anchor: إن في الجنة ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر

RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r7.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says people of affliction receive no scales or register; their reward pours over them, prompting the healthy to wish they had suffered likewise.
RAZI-FULL:v26p221/r7.anchor: روى صاحب ( الكشاف ) عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

STUDYQURAN:39:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r1.claim: The good given to those obedient and righteous in this life may mean Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r1.anchor: Those who are devoutly obedient and perform righteous deeds in this life will receive the gift of Paradise (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:39:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r2.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may mean good in this life, such as health and peace, and in the next.
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r2.anchor: or good in this life (such as health and peace) and in the next (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:39:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r3.speaker: IK, JJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r3.claim: The vastness of God’s earth implies emigrating away from idolaters and encourages the Prophet’s contemporaneous Muslims to leave Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r3.anchor: God’s earth is vast implies that one should emigrate away from the company of idolaters

STUDYQURAN:39:10/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r4.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r4.claim: The “land of God” may refer to the Garden, which one should seek through righteous deeds.
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r4.anchor: the “land of God” in the Garden, which one should seek by performing righteous deeds (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:39:10/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r5.claim: The patient in this verse contrast with those who waver in verse 8.
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r5.anchor: those who are patient contrasts with those who waver in v. 8

STUDYQURAN:39:10/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r6.speaker: Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r6.claim: “Without reckoning” means they will not undergo the weighing of deeds in the Judgment balance.
STUDYQURAN:39:10/r6.anchor: Without reckoning refers to their not having to endure the weighing of their deeds in the balance on the Day of Judgment

TAB-FULL:v20p178/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r1.claim: Believers are told to obey God and avoid disobedience. One interpretation says those who obey receive worldly well-being, with “in this world” attached to the good reward; al-Suddi specifies health and safety.

TAB-FULL:v20p178/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the good reward for those who do good in this world is health and well-being.
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r2.anchor: عن السدي، {للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة} [النحل: 30] قال: «العافية والصحة»

TAB-FULL:v20p178/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r3.claim: A second interpretation attaches “in this world” to “do good” and takes the promised good reward to mean Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v20p178/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون «في» من صلة أحسنوا، ومعنى الحسنة: الجنة

TAB-FULL:v20p179/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p179/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p179/r1.claim: Because God's earth is spacious, believers should emigrate from the land of polytheism to the abode of Islam.
TAB-FULL:v20p179/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وأرض الله واسعة} [الزمر: 10] «فهاجروا واعتزلوا الأوثان»

TAB-FULL:v20p179/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p179/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p179/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the command as emigrating and avoiding idols.
TAB-FULL:v20p179/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وأرض الله واسعة} [الزمر: 10] «فهاجروا واعتزلوا الأوثان»

TAB-FULL:v20p180/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r1.claim: God gives those who patiently endure what they face in this life an afterlife reward without calculation or limit.
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} [الزمر: 10] «لا والله ما هناكم مكيال ولا ميزان»

TAB-FULL:v20p180/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r2.claim: Qatada says their reward has no measure or scale.
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} [الزمر: 10] «لا والله ما هناكم مكيال ولا ميزان»

TAB-FULL:v20p180/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says this unmeasured reward is in Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v20p180/r3.anchor: عن السدي {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} [الزمر: 10] قال: «في الجنة»

ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r5.claim: The reminder that God’s earth is spacious addresses idolaters who should migrate from a place where they are compelled to worship idols, as another verse commands.
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r5.anchor:
ذكر سعة الأرض ههنا لمن كان يعبد الأصنام.
وأمرنا بالمهاجرة عن البلد الذي يكره فيه على عبادتها، كما قال:
(ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها)

ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r6.claim: Those who patiently endure hardship in obedience to God receive reward without measure; tafsir describes it as reward poured out without scale or measure.
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r6.anchor:
(إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب).
أي من صبر على البلاء في طاعة الله أعطي أجره بغير حساب.
جاء في التفسير بغير مكيال وغير ميزان.

ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r7.claim: Spiritual pleasure, joy, and relief cannot literally be weighed; visible measurements are used to help the heart grasp abundance and scarcity.
ZAJJAJ:v4p347/r7.anchor:
مما يتنغم به الإنسان من اللذة والسرور والراحة، فإنه
يمثل ما يعلم بحاسة القلب بما يدرك بالنظر،

TABATABAI:39:10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r1.claim: The promised good is unrestricted: in this life it includes peace of mind, a sound soul, and freedom from worldly confusion and dependence; in the next, lasting happiness and delight.
TABATABAI:39:10/r1.anchor: وقد أطلق الحسنة فلم يقيدها بدنيا أو آخرة وظاهرها ما يعلم الدنيا فللمؤمنين المحسنين في هذه الدنيا طيب النفس وسلامة الروح

TABATABAI:39:10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r2.claim: The alternative grammar attaches in this world to good (hasana); the author says that analysis is not sound.
TABATABAI:39:10/r2.anchor: وقيل { في هذه الدنيا } متعلق بحسنة

TABATABAI:39:10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r3.claim: The wide earth encourages believers to emigrate from Mecca, where persecution and pressure on the Prophet's followers were increasing, though the wording is general.
TABATABAI:39:10/r3.anchor: حث وترغيب لهم في الهجرة من مكة إذ كان التوقف فيها صعبا على المؤمنين بالنبي

TABATABAI:39:10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r4.claim: A reported interpretation takes God's earth as Paradise, which is spacious and has no crowding; obedience earns it, but this reading is remote.
TABATABAI:39:10/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد بأرض الله الجنة أي إن الجنة واسعة لا تزاحم فيها فاكتسبوها بالطاعة والعبادة. وهو بعيد.

TABATABAI:39:10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r5.claim: To give the patient their due fully means the reward is given without reckoning: they are not audited, shown a record, or measured by the scale of their deeds.
TABATABAI:39:10/r5.anchor: لا يعطى الصابرون أجرهم إلا إعطاء بغير حساب، فالصابرون لا يحاسبون على أعمالهم ولا ينشر لهم ديوان ولا يقدر أجرهم

TABATABAI:39:10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r6.claim: The patient are unrestricted in the verse, though the immediate context especially concerns believers enduring worldly hardships inflicted by unbelievers and sinners.
TABATABAI:39:10/r6.anchor: وقد أطلق الصابرون في الآية ولم يقيد بكون الصبر على الطاعة أو عن المعصية أو عند المصيبة

TABATABAI:39:10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:10/r7.claim: Another grammatical view makes without reckoning a circumstantial phrase modifying their reward, meaning an abundant reward; the author prefers the preceding analysis.
TABATABAI:39:10/r7.anchor: ويفيد كثرة الأجر الذي يوفونه، والوجه السابق أقرب.

TABATABAI:39:10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10/r8.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي عن النبي
TABATABAI:39:10/r8.claim: Asked whether wealth given in search of reputation earns reward, the Prophet replied that God accepts only what is offered sincerely, then recited the verse about pure religion.
TABATABAI:39:10/r8.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن يزيد الرقاشي أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله إنا نعطي أموالنا التماس الذكر فهل لنا في

TABATABAI:39:10#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله
TABATABAI:39:10#2/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says people afflicted with trials have a scale but no record when records are spread and scales set; the Prophet recited the promise that the patient are fully rewarded without reckoning.
TABATABAI:39:10#2/r8.anchor: روى العياشي بالإسناد عن عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله

TABATABAI:39:10#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:10#2/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي
TABATABAI:39:10#2/r9.claim: The author notes the same report is transmitted in al-Durr al-Manthur from Anas and the Prophet.
TABATABAI:39:10#2/r9.anchor: في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في حديث.

TABRISI:39:9-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:9-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:9-10/r10.claim: The address is to those who affirm God's unity; fearing their Lord means avoiding His punishment by refraining from disobedience, and the clause ends there.

TABRISI:39:9-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:9-10/r11.speaker: author
