TABRISI:39:9-10/r11.claim: Those who do good perform virtuous acts and kindness to others; al-Suddī says their worldly good includes praise, good reputation, thanks, health, and safety.
TABRISI:39:9-10/r11.anchor: أي فعلوا الأعمال الحسنة وأحسنوا إلى غيرهم

TABRISI:39:9-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:9-10/r12.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:39:9-10/r12.claim: Al-Suddī lists good reputation, praise, gratitude, health, and safety as their worldly reward.
TABRISI:39:9-10/r12.anchor: ثناء حسن وذكر جميل ومدح وشكر وصحة وسلامة عن السدي

TABRISI:39:9-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:9-10/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:9-10/r13.claim: Another view makes good deeds in this world the cause of an afterlife reward: permanent residence in Paradise.
TABRISI:39:9-10/r13.anchor: للذين أحسنوا العمل في هذه الدنيا مثوبة حسنة في الآخرة وهو الخلود في الجنة

TABRISI:39:9-10/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:9-10/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:39:9-10/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the spacious earth as encouragement to emigrate from Mecca when unable to obey God there; another land may permit it.
TABRISI:39:9-10/r14.anchor: هذا حث لهم على الهجرة من مكة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:39:10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:10/r1.speaker: مقاتل، أبو مسلم
TABRISI:39:10/r1.claim: Another interpretation makes the broad earth Paradise, which people should seek through righteous deeds.
TABRISI:39:10/r1.anchor: وأرض الله الجنة واسعة فاطلبوها بالأعمال الصالحة عن مقاتل وأبي مسلم

TABRISI:39:10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:10/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:10/r2.claim: The patient receive the reward for obedience and enduring worldly hardships without reckoning because it is too abundant to count.

TABRISI:39:10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:10/r3.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:39:10/r3.claim: The Prophet says that no scale is set up and no record spread for the afflicted when records and balances are brought out; he then recites this verse.
TABRISI:39:10/r3.anchor:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إذا نشرت الدواوين ونصبت الموازين

ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n16/r1.claim: Asad supplies “God speaks” because the possessive in “servants of Mine” refers to God.
ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n16/r1.anchor: the possessive pronoun in the subsequent phrase "servants of Mine" obviously relates to God

ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n17/r1.claim: God’s earth being wide means people can always do good and spiritually migrate from evil toward God; Asad links this enduring sense of hijrah to 4:97.
ASAD-NOTES:39:10#n17/r1.anchor: there is always a possibility of doing good and "migrating from evil unto God" - which is the permanent, spiritual connotation

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:8-10/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:8-10/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:8-10/r3.claim: Those excelling in this life are monotheists who obey God, and their reward is Paradise. They should migrate away from disbelievers; the patient receive reward without measure.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r1.claim: Faith is indispensable to being Muslim, while the verse also presents God-consciousness and goodness as conditions of good Muslim life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r1.anchor: Müslüman sayılmanın vazgeçilmez şartı iman etmektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r2.claim: Taqwa is reverent responsibility and careful obedience that protects against divine punishment; hasana spans every virtue and good state, beginning with sound belief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r2.anchor: Takvâ, Allah’a sorumluluk bilinciyle saygı gösterip buyruklarını titizlikle yerine getirmek suretiyle ilâhî cezadan korunmayı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r3.claim: Exegetes usually limit the good promised in return for goodness to paradise, but the author prefers all worldly and afterlife good and happiness because the verse sets no limit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r3.anchor: Tefsirlerde çoğunlukla, karşılık olarak verilecek bu iyilik cennet olarak açıklanmışsa da âyette böyle bir sınırlama olmadığına göre

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r4.speaker: zayıf bir görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r4.claim: A minority, weak view takes God's spacious earth to mean paradise; exegetes generally understand it as a reference to migration.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r4.anchor: müfessirler genellikle bu ifadeyi hicrete işaret olarak anlamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r5.claim: Muslims should work for conditions allowing religious and virtuous life and value such freedom; when they cannot live their values or improve conditions, they should move somewhere they can.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r5.anchor: inançlı ve erdemli olarak yaşayabileceği düzeyde bir özgürlük ortamının oluşması için çaba göstermesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r6.claim: This relocation may range from changing jobs to moving countries; the Prophet and companions migrated from Mecca to Medina after efforts failed to secure religious freedom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r6.anchor: Hz. Peygamber ve arkadaşları, bütün çabalarına rağmen Mekke’de dinlerini yaşama özgürlüğünü sağlayamayınca Allah’ın emri uyarınca Medine’ye göç etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r7.claim: Sacrificing for one's values takes great patience and resolve, so the verse promises the patient a reward without measure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:10/r7.anchor: İnsanın değerleri uğruna böylesine bir özveriyi göze alması büyük bir sabır ve kararlılık işi olduğu için

IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r1.claim: Abu Amr pauses on عباد at an āya ending but reads عباد الذين with the yāʾ when the phrase continues; his reading is described as pausal separation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r1.anchor: وقال عبيد عن أبى عمرو إن كانت رأس آية وقفت ﴿ عباد ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r2.speaker: قنبل عن النبال عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r2.claim: Qunbul transmits from Ibn Kathir عبادِ الذين without the yāʾ, with kasra on dāl; the other readers also omit the yāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r2.anchor: وقرأت على قنبل عن النبال عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير ﴿ عباد ﴾ الذين ) بكسر الدال من غير ياء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r1.claim: The Messenger is told to exhort believers to piety and convey the command in God's own words, honoring them by calling them His servants and strengthening the command's force.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r1.anchor: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يذكر المؤمنين ويحملهم على التقوى والطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r2.claim: The promise to those who do good explains the command or its binding force; “good” is indefinite for magnification, and the good promised is Paradise in the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r2.anchor: تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الامتثال به والجار والمجرور متعلق بمحذوف هو خبر مقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r3.claim: The phrase “in this world” modifies doing good, while “good” is an emphatic indefinite subject; the earth's breadth is an aside removing lack of opportunity in one's homeland as an excuse for neglect.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r3.anchor: في هذه الدنيا متعلق بأحسنوا واسم الإشارة للإحضار

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r4.claim: The clause about the patient continues the parenthetical explanation, contrasting the promised good with the special unlimited recompense of patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248/r4.anchor: إنما يوفى الصابرون أجورهم بغير حساب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r1.claim: The aside explains that those unable to obey properly in their homeland should move elsewhere and migrate toward God for His approval; in that cause, every hardship is outweighed by its reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r1.anchor: فليتحولوا إن لم يتمكنوا عنها وليهاجروا إلى ربهم لنيل الرضوان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r2.claim: The promised special recompense answers whether migrants and those able to obey at home are equal: patient migrants forsake attachments and follow prophets and the righteous, receiving immeasurable reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r2.anchor: الذين صبروا على الهجرة ومفارقة المحاب والاقتداء بالأنبياء والصالحين أجرهم بغير حساب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r3.claim: The shift to passive voice stresses patience as the cause of reward and implies the addressees will likewise be repaid for their patience, as earlier people were.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r3.anchor: وعدل عنه إلى المنزل تنبيها على أن المقتضى لذلك صبرهم فيفيد أنكم توفون أجوركم بصبركم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r4.claim: Although prompted here by migration, patience and the unrestricted recompense cover every affliction; “without reckoning” can modify the reward or the patient people and is primarily hyperbole for abundance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r4.anchor: وهو محمول على العموم شامل للصبر على كل بلاء غير مخصوص بالصبر على المهاجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains reward without reckoning as so abundant that no accountant can reach or comprehend its measure.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r5.anchor: قول ابن عباس لا يهتدي إليه حساب الحساب ولا يعرف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r6.claim: A less immediate grammatical possibility makes “without reckoning” describe the patient people: they are not reckoned at all, though the apparent sense is abundant reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r6.anchor: وجوز جعل الحال من الصابرين على معنى لا يحاسبون أصلا والمتبادر ما يفيد المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r7.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi links “in this world” semantically to “good,” rather than to doing good.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r7.anchor: عن السدي أن قوله تعالى ( في الدنيا ) متعلق بحسنة من حيث المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r8.claim: Alusi notes grammatical objections to treating the phrase as a circumstantial modifier of the indefinite subject “good”; making it a subject governed by the adverb only works on al-Akhfash's weak position.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r8.anchor: ورد بأنها مبتدأ ولا يجوز الحال منه على الصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads “in this world” as an explanatory gloss for “good”: the good is health and well-being in worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : هو بيان لحسنة والتقدير هي في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r10.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r10.claim: Al-Kashf says the explanatory reading suits the meaning better than a restrictive circumstantial reading: worldly health is a small immediate benefit, while full recompense comes in the next life.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r10.anchor: قال في الكشف : وإنما آثر كونه بيانا مع جواز كونه حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r11.claim: On that alternative, the earth's breadth removes objections based on differing climates and bodily conditions; worldly health is an immediate share, whereas full limitless reward belongs to the patient, consoling sufferers and encouraging worship and obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r11.anchor: وفي ذلك تسلية لأهل البلاء وتنشيط للعباد على مكابدة العبادات وتحريض على ملازمة الطاعات

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r12.claim: Alusi calls the alternative fine but prefers the primary reading: the context more directly removes inability to obey at home as an excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r12.anchor: أحدهما أن الإعتراض لإزاحة العلة في التفريط أظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r13.claim: The primary reading also matches Quranic injunctions to migrate when God's earth is constricted, and normally a prepositional phrase attaches to the closest suitable expression absent a contrary reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p248#2/r13.anchor: من نحو ( ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r1.claim: A further objection to the health reading is that worldly health can benefit unbelievers too; calling it divine entrapment is unconvincing given the verse about people claiming worldly good as their due.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r1.anchor: فإن الحسنة بذلك المعنى في شأن المخالفين أتم والقول بأنها استدراج في شأنهم لا حسنة ليس بالظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r2.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r2.claim: Al-Tabarsi transmits al-Suddi's gloss of worldly good as good reputation and favorable mention, as well as health and safety.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r2.anchor: والذي نقله الطبرسي عن السدي تفسير الحسنة في الدنيا بالثناء الحسن والذكر الجميل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r3.claim: Some interpret the promised good as God's guardianship, which unbelievers do not share.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r3.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم بولاية الله تعالى وعليه فليس للمخالفين منها نصيب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r4.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r4.claim: Ata says God's earth here means Medina; on that view, doing good means emigrating and the worldly good is relief from enemies.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r4.anchor: فعن عطاء أرض الله تعالى المدينة قال أبو حيان : فعلى هذا يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r5.claim: Abu Muslim allows “God's earth” to mean Paradise, supporting the reading that the good of the next life is eternal residence there.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : لا يمتنع ذلك لأنه تعالى أمر المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the interpretation of God's earth as Paradise arbitrary and unsupported.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r6.anchor: وتعقبه ابن عطية بأنه تحكم لا دليل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r7.claim: Alusi prefers the first interpretation: “good” includes good things in both worldly and next life, while ihsan means inward and outward good action.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r7.anchor: والرجحان لما سمعت أولا واختير فيه شمول الحسنة لحسنات الدنيا والآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r8.claim: Ihsan is worshipping God as if seeing Him, or at least knowing He sees the worshipper, according to the Prophet's explanation in the Gabriel report.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r8.anchor: في حديث جبريل عليه السلام أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r9.claim: Some transmitted accounts say the verse was revealed about Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib and his companions when they resolved to migrate to Abyssinia.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r9.anchor: والآية على ما في بعض الآثار نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب وأصحابه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r10.claim: The verse highlights the great merit of those who remain patient.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p249/r10.anchor: وفيها من الدلالة على فضل الصابرين ما فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r1.claim: Fearing God means obeying Him and avoiding disobedience; those who do good are believers who act well.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r1.anchor: اتقوا ربكم} بطاعته واجتناب معصيته، {للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا} أي: آمنوا وأحسنوا العمل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r2.claim: Muqatil identifies the good promised in this world as Paradise.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r3.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the good as health and well-being in this world.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: في هذه الدنيا حسنة يعني: الصحة والعافية،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets God's wide earth as an instruction to leave Mecca, urging migration away from places where sin is open.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني ارتحلوا من مكة. وفيه حث على الهجرة من البلد الذي يظهر فيه المعاصي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r5.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about the migrants to Abyssinia.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r6.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says anyone commanded to commit sins should flee.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: من أمر بالمعاصي فليهرب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r7.claim: The patient held to their religion and did not abandon it because of persecution.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r7.anchor: {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} الذين صبروا على دينهم فلم يتركوه للأذى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r8.claim: Another report says the verse concerns Jaafar ibn Abi Talib and his companions, who endured severe trials, kept their religion, and migrated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r8.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب وأصحابه، حيث لم يتركوا دينهم لما اشتد بهم البلاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r9.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r9.claim: Ali says every obedient person receives a measured reward, while the patient are rewarded in heaps.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r9.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: كل مطيع يكال له كيلا ويوزن له وزنا إلا الصابرون، فإنه يحثى لهم حثيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r10.claim: A report says people afflicted with trials will have no scale or record; their reward will be poured on them without reckoning, making people of ease wish their bodies had been cut because of that merit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p111/r10.anchor: يؤتى بأهل البلاء فلا ينصب لهم ميزان ولا ينشر لهم ديوان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r1.claim: Taqwā here means adhering to God's obedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r2.claim: Doing good through worldly obedience brings a good afterlife reward; another reading makes the good health and well-being in this world, with the phrase locating it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r2.anchor: أي للذين أحسنوا بالطاعات في الدنيا مثوبة حسنة في الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r3.claim: The earth's breadth permits anyone unable to practice goodness in their homeland to migrate to somewhere they can.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r3.anchor: فمن تعسر عليه التوفر على الإحسان في وطنه فليهاجر

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r4.claim: The patient endure hardship in obedience, trials, and migration; their reward exceeds what any reckoning can comprehend.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r4.anchor: على مشاق الطاعات من احتمال البلاء ومهاجرة الأوطان لها

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r5.speaker: حديث
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r5.claim: A report says scales are set for prayer, charity, and pilgrimage, but afflicted people receive reward poured on them without measure, until the healthy wish for their trial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:10/r5.anchor: ولا ينصب لأهل البلاء بل يصب عليهم الأجر صبا حتى يتمنى أهل العافية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to steady believers against numerous opponents by addressing them as God’s servants, an intimate possessive that reassures them of His nearness and honors them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r1.anchor: يا عباد الله , مثلا تذكيرا لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r2.claim: Belief may exist at its lowest degree without full God-consciousness; ‘fear your Lord’ calls the graced believers to deepen obedience and sincerity, rooting faith and excellence without implying God needs anything.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r2.anchor: وهذا أدل دليل على أن الإيمان يكون مع عدم التقوى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r3.claim: The author prefers reading ‘for those who excel in this world, a good reward’ as covering good in this life and the Hereafter; an alternative makes only the worldly reward the predicate, unduly limiting the promise.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r3.anchor: أوقعوا الإحسان , ومعلوم أنه في هذه الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p428/r4.claim: An alternative parsing takes aḥsanū to mean ‘did good,’ with ‘in this world’ introducing a new subject-predicate clause; the author rejects it as confined to worldly reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r1.claim: If one’s land obstructs obedience and encourages sin, one should migrate; every land is equally under God’s knowledge and power, so staying put is no excuse for neglecting excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r1.anchor: على الهجرة إلى حيث يزول عنه ذلك المانع

BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r2.claim: Patience through migration and separation from home or family earns an immeasurable reward: other deeds can be counted, but patience continues with every breath and varies in hidden strength and effects.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r2.anchor: أي على ما تكرهه النفوس في مخالفة الهوى واتباع أوامر الملك الأعلى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r3.claim: Alternatively, perfect patience may mean no reckoning at all; al-Bazzār and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ transmit from Abū Hurayra that a woman asked the Prophet for a cure and chose patience when told she could have either, receiving no reckoning.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p429/r3.anchor: لما رواه البزار وابن حبان في صحيحه عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v7p213/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p213/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p213/r10.claim: 'God's earth is vast' means believers should migrate and leave the idols.
DURR-FULL:v7p213/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وأرض الله واسعة} قال: أرضي واسعة فهاجروا واعتزلوا الأوثان

DURR-FULL:v7p215/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r1.claim: The patient receive reward without measure or scale.
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حسا

DURR-FULL:v7p215/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r2.claim: The patient receive more than a reward merely counted according to their deeds.
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} قال: بلغني أنه لا يحسب عليهم ثواب عملهم ولكن يزادون

DURR-FULL:v7p215/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r3.claim: God may intensify trials for a beloved servant to hear his supplication, then grant it, save it for later, or avert worse harm. The afflicted receive reward without weighing, making the spared wish they had suffered.
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r3.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن الله إذا أحب عبدا أو أراد أن يصافيه

DURR-FULL:v7p215/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r4.claim: A tree of affliction in Paradise signifies that the afflicted receive reward without a register or scale.
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي رضى الله عنه قال: سمعت جدي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن في الجنة شجرة

DURR-FULL:v7p215/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r5.claim: On Resurrection Day, those who suffered trials will wish their skins had been cut with scissors.
DURR-FULL:v7p215/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: يود أهل البلاء يوم القيامة أن جلودهم كانت تقرض بالمقاريض

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:11/r2.claim: Verse 10 condenses Muslim duties, from sound belief and worship to good character, into faith, God-consciousness, and goodness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:11/r2.anchor: 10. âyette iyi bir müslüman olmanın şartları, doğru inançtan ibadetlere ve güzel ahlâka kadar bütün İslâmî yükümlülükleri kapsayan şu üç kelimeyle özetlenmişti: İman, takvâ, hasene (iyilik).

ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r11.claim: The believing servants are those who believe in God out of longing; they are told to fear Him and seek no other.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r11.anchor: ( قل يا عبادي الذين آمنوا ) بي شوقا إلى اتقوا ربكم فلا تطلبوا غيره سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r12.claim: Those who do good in seeking God seek no one besides Him, and their reward is the supreme blessing of finding Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r12.anchor: للذين أحسنوا في طلبي في هذه الدنيا بأن لم يطلبوا مني غيري ( حسنة ) عظيمة وهي حسنة وجداني

ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r13.claim: The vast earth alludes to the limitless domain of divine majesty and beauty, where spiritual realization has no endpoint.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r13.anchor: وأرض الله واسعة وهي حضيرة جلاله وجماله فإنها لا نهاية لها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r14.claim: The patient receive manifestations without measure because God's manifestations are endless, as indicated by the statement that He is occupied with a new affair every day.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r14.anchor: إنما يوفى الصابرون على صدق الطلب أجرهم من التجليات بغير حساب إذ لا نهاية لتجلياته تعالى وكل يوم هو في شأن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r1.speaker: الهروي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r1.claim: Al-Harawi's Gharībayn defines al-mabwaʾ as an established dwelling and an earth or place where one settles and feels at home.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r1.anchor: وفى الغريبين للهروى (باب الباء مع الواو) والمبوأ المنزل الملزوم، وأرض مباءة منزولة مألوفة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r2.claim: The root suggests settling in a suitable, secure position; the Prophet placed believers in battle stations he judged safer, more defensible, and suited to their ability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p593/r2.anchor: يبدو أن التمكن من المنزل الملائم والموقع المنيع، ملحوظ فى الدلالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p768/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p768/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p768/r2.claim: The two passages differ in many respects, not only the yāʾ in ʿibādī; each Qur'anic deletion and addition is deliberate and belongs in its context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p768/r2.anchor: والتعبير القرآني مقصود وكل حذف وإضافة مقصود أن يوضع في مكانه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r1.claim: The shorter ʿibādi form suits a smaller group, while the longer ʿibādī suits a broader group; he links word length with group size.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1059/r1.anchor: كلما يقول عبادي يكون أكثر من عبادِ مناسبة لسعة الكلمة وطولها وسعة المجموعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p887/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p887/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p887/r1.claim: Gratitude should be more frequent than patience because blessings persist at every moment, whereas patience is needed at particular acts or occasional hardships.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p887/r1.anchor: الشكر يجب أن يكون أكثر من الصبر فالصبر يكون كما أسلفنا إما عند الطاعات وهي لها أوقات محددة

JISHUMI:v2p1070/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1070/r1.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v2p1070/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the destination as a place where no one but God judges, like saying that a matter was referred to the prince.
JISHUMI:v2p1070/r1.anchor: الموضع الذي لا حاكم سواه، كقولهم: رفع أمرنا إلى الأمير، عن أبي علي

BAQILLANI:v1p234/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r1.claim: The opening line is disconnected from what precedes and offers only familiar paronomasia, so its repeated wordplay is not truly novel.
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r1.anchor: فالبيت الأول منقطع عما قبله وليس فيه شئ غير التجنيس الذي ليس ببديع لتكرره على كل لسان

BAQILLANI:v1p234/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r2.claim: The phrase about one distance following another is pleasing, but its device is well-worn; the second line is close to its predecessor in wording and meaning, and saying that good is not done unhurriedly is poor diction.
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r2.anchor: ما أخذ المدى بعد المدى فإنه لفظ مليح

BAQILLANI:v1p234/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r3.claim: The image of pulling stars down with reins is extremely objectionable; the following line is unrelated, opens badly, and uses an unmotivated interrogative turn.
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r3.anchor: فالبيت الأول منكر جدا في جر النجوم بالأرسان من موضعه إلى العلو والتكلف فيه واقع

BAQILLANI:v1p234/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r4.claim: The two lines are alien to the poem, and the panegyric that follows with a pledge of self-sacrifice and a wish to meet Abu Sa'id does not sound like the poet's style.
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r4.anchor: والبيتان أجنبيان من كلامه غريبان في قصيدته ولم يقع له في المدح في هذه القصيدة شئ جيد

BAQILLANI:v1p234/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r5.claim: The threat naming Mudar, Rabia, and Azd has a good meaning, but place names prevent stylistic refinement; the same idea is expressed better in the line about all people becoming angry when Banu Tamim are.
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r5.anchor: البيت الأول حسن المعنى وإن كانت ألفاظه بذكر الأماكن لا يتأتى فيه التحسين

BAQILLANI:v1p234/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r6.claim: The next line is poorly joined to what precedes and clumsy in diction; forced rhyme and genealogy spoil the poem.
BAQILLANI:v1p234/r6.anchor: والبيت الثاني قد تعذر عليه وصله بما سبق من الكلام على وجه يلطف وهو قبيح اللفظ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r1.claim: An unnamed poem illustrates night as estrangement and oppressive weight, then imagines stars as pilgrims cutting through darkness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r1.anchor: رب ليل قطعته كالصدود وفراق ما كان فيه وداع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r2.claim: A poet likens escape from hardship to the moon emerging from clouds; hardship, cloud, and darkness resemble one another rationally, not by the senses.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r2.anchor: الشبه بين البأساء والغمام والظلماء من طريق العقل لا من طريق الحس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r3.claim: Jurjani calls Ibn Tabataba's comparison clearer: clear sky and light with cloud and darkness resemble joy interrupted by grief.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r3.anchor: وأوضح منه في هذا القول ابن طباطبا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r4.claim: Jurjani explains the Tanukhi image of fire and coal as justice and injustice: justice is conventionally bright, while injustice is its dark opposite.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r4.anchor: فإنه لما كان يقال في الحق إنه منير واضح لائح فتستعار له أوصاف الأجسام المنيرة وفي الظلم خلاف ذلك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r5.claim: Ibn Babak compares a road to a generous man's character because moral qualities are often described as wide or narrow, making the metaphor seem literal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r5.anchor: لما كانت الأخلاق توصف بالسعة والضيق وكثر ذلك واستمر توهمه حقيقة فقابل بين سعة الأرض

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r6.claim: Abu Talib al-Ma'muni compares a barren plain's real breadth with aspirations; familiar phrases about long, boundless hopes make their metaphorical breadth seem sensory.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r6.anchor: ولكن لما كان يقال آمال طوال وآمال لا نهاية لها واتسعت آماله وأشباه ذلك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r7.claim: Jurjani introduces another subtle Ibn Tabataba comparison based on darkness and blackness rather than spaciousness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p200/r7.anchor: ولكن في الظلمة والاسوداد قول ابن طباطبا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r1.claim: If rhetorical merit lay in verbal sequence alone, everyone hearing the same sequence would judge its quality equally; actual differences in judgment refute that view.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r1.anchor: لكان ينبغي ألا يختلف حال اثنين في العلم بحسن النظم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r2.claim: Because composition is a craft requiring thought, its object is what the thinker works upon; a builder cannot think about spinning and thereby build with bricks.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r2.anchor: لو جاز ذلك لجاز أن يفكر البناء في الغزل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r3.claim: Words follow the order of meanings in the mind because they signify and contain them; no separate act of thought is needed to arrange words after meanings are ordered.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p57/r3.anchor: فإذا وجب لمعنى أن يكون أولا في النفس وجب اللفظ الدال عليه أن يكون مثله أولا في النطق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r1.claim: Al-arḍ is the familiar word for earth and is named for its breadth or expansiveness.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt says a sore is said to أرض when it expands.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r2.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : أرضت القرحة أرضا بفتح الراء : إذا اتسعت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r3.claim: Ibn Faris says every broad thing can be called أرض, and a man أريض is well suited for good.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r3.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : كل ما اتسع أرض ورجل أريض للخير : أي : خليق له

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r4.claim: الأرضة is a small termite-like creature, and خشبة مأروضة is wood eaten by termites.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r4.anchor: والأرضة دويبة وخشبة مأروضة : أكلتها الأرضة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r5.claim: الإرض denotes a large carpet or spread made of wool or hair.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r5.anchor: والإرض . بساط ضخم من وبر أو صوف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r6.claim: The expression يتأرض لي means يتعرض لي, to approach or present oneself to me.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r6.anchor: وجاء فلان يتأرض [ لي ] مثل يتعرض لي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r7.claim: فلان ابن أرض is said of a stranger or foreigner.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r7.anchor: ويقال : فلان ابن أرض إذا كان غريبا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r8.claim: أرض أريضة describes land with healthy, abundant vegetation.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas is quoted as contrasting the earth's trembling with a feeling of shaking within oneself.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس . أزلزلت الأرض أم بي أرض

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r10.claim: One Qur'anic sense is the land of Paradise, as in the inheritance promised to God's righteous servants and the believers' inheritance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r10.anchor: أحدها : أرض الجنة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنبياء : ﴿ أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r11.claim: A second sense is the land of Mecca, illustrated by the people who say they were oppressed in the land and by the land losing territory at its edges.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r11.anchor: والثاني : أرض مكة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء : ﴿ قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r12.claim: A third sense is the land of Medina, cited in migration passages and in the command that God's earth is wide.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r12.anchor: والثالث : أرض المدينة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء : ^ ( [ قالوا ] ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r13.claim: A fourth sense is the land of Syria, identified with the blessed land to which Abraham and Lot were delivered and the territory inherited by the oppressed people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p167/r13.anchor: والرابع : أرض الشام . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف : ^ ( وأورثنا القوم الذين كانوا يستضعفون

ITQAN:v1p52/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p52/r5.speaker: السخاوي
ITQAN:v1p52/r5.claim: Al-Sakhawi records that some add the verse addressing believing servants to al-Zumar’s Medinan exceptions.
ITQAN:v1p52/r5.anchor: الآية ذكره السخاوي في جمال القراء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r2.claim: The contrast between all souls tasting death and the smaller number of patient people supports the author’s association of explicit yā with a larger group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r2.anchor: أما في الثانية فهنا الصابرون وهؤلاء أقل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r1.claim: In 29:56, possessives for God's servants and land plus إن emphasize the land's vastness; 39:10 says God's earth is vast without extra emphasis because it is unnecessary there.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r1.anchor: العباد عباده والأرض أرضه ولإضافة الياء إلى كلمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r2.claim: The universal death and return statement fits the broad address to God's servants in Ankabut, while the few patient people in Zumar fit its narrower class of servants.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r2.anchor: الصابرون هم قلة فناسب سياق الآية كلها الطبقة القليلة مع عباد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r3.claim: Ankabut repeats first-person divine pronouns five times in the passage, while Zumar's address omits the possessive first-person suffix.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r3.anchor: ضمير المتكلم تكرر 5 مرات في سورة العنكبوت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r4.claim: Ankabut maintains first-person divine speech through its context; Zumar uses indirect third-person relay through قل, a pattern that continues through its two procession verses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p770/r4.anchor: آية سورة العنكبوت مبنية على التكلّم بينما آية سورة الزمر مبنية على الغيبة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r1.speaker: المفسرون
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r1.claim: One reported interpretation attaches “without reckoning” to the reward: it is poured out abundantly, emphasizing the great measure of the reward.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r1.anchor: والمفسرون يفسرونها أحد تفسيرين: إما أن الأجر يُصبّ عليهم صباً بغير حساب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r2.speaker: المفسرون
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r2.claim: The other interpretation attaches the phrase to the patient: they receive reward without being called to account, with their sins forgiven and Paradise granted without reckoning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r2.anchor: والمفسرون يفسرونها أحد تفسيرين: إما أن الأجر يُصبّ عليهم صباً بغير حساب للدلالة على المبالغة في الأجر، أو أن الصابرين يصب عليهم الأجر ولا يحاسبون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r3.speaker: رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r3.claim: The cited hadith says that seventy thousand from the Prophet's community will enter Paradise without reckoning; the author gives no grading.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p910/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث الشريف عن سول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:"سبعون ألفاً من أمتي يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب"

NASHR:v2p140/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r1.speaker: أبو العلاء الهمداني عن رويس
NASHR:v2p140/r1.claim: This route uniquely affirms the yāʾ in يا عباد الذين آمنوا at pause, by analogy with يا عباد فاتقون.
NASHR:v2p140/r1.anchor: وانفرد أبو العلاء الهمداني عن رويس بإثبات يا عباد الذين آمنوا. أول الزمر في الوقف، وخالف سائر الرواة

NASHR:v2p362#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p362#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p362#2/r2.claim: At pause, readers unanimously delete the yāʾ in يا عبادي except for the reading uniquely reported by al-Hafiz Abu al-Ala from Ruways.
NASHR:v2p362#2/r2.anchor: الوقف عليها بالحذف إجماع إلا ما انفرد به الحافظ أبو العلا عن رويس
